correctness.rationale: The Katz–Kleiman conormal formula gives dual degree de times the cubic complete homogeneous polynomial in d-1 and e-1. With q=d+e-2 and s=e-d, algebra reduces this to a constant in q minus (q/8)(s squared minus 2(q+1)) squared. Thus the optimizer is exactly the admissible parity-lattice square nearest to 2(q+1). Adjacent admissible gaps tie iff 2q=s(s+2), forcing s=2k and q=2k(k+1), with the stated bidegrees. Mesh-two approximation gives the square-root asymptotic. Fresh exact enumeration through q=2000 reproduced every optimizer and the tie sequence.

final_claim: For smooth codimension-two complete-intersection threefolds X_(d,e) in projective five-space with fixed d+e, projective-dual degree is maximized exactly when the parity-compatible gap s=e-d makes s squared nearest to 2(d+e-1); the maximizer is unique except for q=d+e-2=2k(k+1), where two explicit adjacent bidegrees tie, and maximizing gaps are asymptotic to sqrt(2q).
limitations: Smooth complex codimension-two threefold complete intersections only.
No extension to singular varieties, other dimensions or higher codimension is claimed.
